reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds, so I'll start by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (order 181 for 17092 and order 184 for 3930), so I can proceed. Next I need the list of customers to pay, so I'll call list_orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly, so I can proceed. The orders cover three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance before recording any payout.
acme's net balance is 27136, which matches its orders: 16857 + 10279 = 27136 with no refunds against acme. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
birch's net is 19909, which matches 26275 + 14656 minus the refunds 17092 + 3930 = 19909. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
Cobalt's net is 31469, which matches its orders 26600 + 4869 with no refunds. All three balances check out against the orders and refunds, so I'll record the first payout, acme for 27136.
acme's payout of 27136 is recorded. I verified birch's net of 19909 against its orders and the matching refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout of 19909 is recorded. Cobalt's net of 31469 matches its orders (26600 + 4869) with no refunds, so I'll record that last payout.
All three customers have been paid. The refunds table matched Alpha's report, and each payout equals the net_balance figure, which I checked against the orders and refunds.
